title: Inventing Reality
author: Michael Parenti
desc: Cómo los medios fabrican la realidad política. Propaganda mediática diseccionada.
tesis: Los medios de comunicación no reflejan la realidad — la inventan. Parenti demuestra con ejemplos concretos cómo los grandes medios estadounidenses seleccionan, enmarcan, distorsionan y silencian información para servir a los intereses del capital corporativo. No se trata de 'errores' o 'sesgo' sino de un sistema estructural: los medios son propiedad de corporaciones, dependen de publicidad corporativa y están integrados a la élite de poder.
ideas: Los medios no 'reflejan' la realidad sino que la construyen: seleccionan qué se discute, cómo se enmarca, y qué se silencia.
La concentración de la propiedad mediática en pocas corporaciones no es un problema accesorio — es el mecanismo central de control ideológico.
La 'objetividad' periodística es una ficción útil: todos los medios tienen perspectiva, pero solo los corporativos pueden pretender que no la tienen.
contexto: Primera edición publicada en 1986, segunda edición revisada en 1993. Contemporáneo y complemento de Manufacturing Consent de Chomsky/Herman (1988). Donde Chomsky construye un modelo abstracto de propaganda, Parenti documenta caso por caso cómo los medios distorsionan la cobertura de guerras, huelgas, elecciones y movimientos sociales.

conexiones.razon: Los medios fabrican el consenso que hace funcionar la 'democracia para los pocos'.
Los medios que Inventing Reality denuncia son los que justifican el imperio que Against Empire documenta.

quotes.text: The major distortions are repeatable and systemic — the product not only of deliberate manipulation but of the ideological and economic conditions under which the media operate.

tl: Francia coloniza Vietnam con apoyo gringo silenciado
From 1945 to 1954 the United States spent several billion dollars supporting a ruthless French colonialism in Vietnam, but the American public was never informed of this.
cap. 9, sec. The Vietnam Apology
EU asume la dictadura de Vietnam del Sur

Washington assumed full responsibility for the maintenance of the South Vietnamese right-wing dictatorship, but the public neither read nor heard a word of debate in the media about this major policy commitment.
cap. 9, sec. The Vietnam Apology
Escalada masiva de tropas en Vietnam, 1965

In 1965 the US government began a massive build-up of ground forces in Vietnam, but Americans were told that the troops were merely a small support force. The New York Times and other major news agencies knew the real nature of the escalation but felt it was in the national interest to keep this information from the public.
cap. 9, sec. The Vietnam Apology
Masacre de Tlatelolco

The My Lai massacre of over one hundred unarmed Vietnamese women, children, and elderly men by US troops was not publicized until over a year after it happened, and then by a small independent news service.
cap. 9, sec. The Vietnam Apology
Triunfo electoral de la Unidad Popular en Chile

In 1970, when a socialist candidate, Salvador Allende, was elected president of Chile and began initiating reforms, that country suddenly became the hottest news story in Latin America. From the beginning the US press saw the democratically elected government as an ominous threat to democracy.
cap. 9, sec. Murder in Chile
Newsweek censura matanza más grande que My Lai

The murder of Vietnamese civilians on a much larger scale than My Lai was documented by two Newsweek correspondents in 1971. Newsweek refused to print their story for six months and would not release it for freelance submission to other publications.
cap. 9, sec. The Vietnam Apology
Nixon manda hacer gritar a la economía chilena

The United States eagerly assisted in this campaign to make the economy scream (President Nixon's phrase) by cutting off food aid, denying Chile any new loans, and cutting exports to Chile by some 40 percent and imports from that country almost by half.
cap. 9, sec. Murder in Chile
Golpe contra Allende en septiembre de 1973

The democratic government was overthrown in September 1973, in a violent coup led by right-wing generals who abolished the constitution, suppressed all political parties, closed all newspapers except two right-wing dailies, outlawed all independent trade unions, and arrested, tortured, and executed thousands of persons.
cap. 9, sec. Murder in Chile
Asesinato de 65 periodistas en El Salvador y Guatemala

Nor did the press take much note of the sixty-five reporters who, according to the Committee to Protect Journalists, were murdered by government-allied death squads in El Salvador and Guatemala during the mid-1980s.
cap. 10, sec. Looking One Way for Suppression
Guerra de los contras y embargo contra Nicaragua

US forces mined Nicaragua's harbors, blew up its oil depots, and openly armed, trained, and financed a mercenary army of contras, who engaged in a premeditated war of bloody attrition to terrorize civilian noncombatants.
cap. 10, sec. The Totalitarian Sandinistas
Invasión de Granada celebrada como rescate, 1983

In 1983, when the US government invaded the tiny and relatively defenseless sovereign nation of Grenada (population 110,000), in an unprovoked assault and in blatant violation of international law, killing scores of the island's occupants and defenders, the American press pretty much went along with it.
cap. 9, sec. Stomping on Grenada
Sandinistas ganan elecciones limpias en 1984

Some 460 official foreign observers from all over the world, who were free to check all aspects of the voting process and ballot counting, agreed that with the exception of a few incidents, the campaign was fair, honest, and noncoercive.
cap. 10, sec. The Totalitarian Sandinistas
Invasión gringa de Panamá en diciembre de 1989

On December 20, 1989, President Bush ordered US forces to attack Panama. Television news, the medium reaching the largest audiences, provided coverage of Operation Just Cause that resembled a US Army recruitment film.
cap. 10, sec. A Devil in Panama
Glaspie da luz verde a Saddam antes de Kuwait
Shortly before the invasion, Hussein had received assurances from April Glaspie, the US ambassador in Baghdad, that the United States had no interest in Iraq's dispute with Kuwait.
cap. 10, sec. Celebrating the Massacre of Iraq
Mentira de los bebés en incubadoras kuwaitíes

One of the media's favorite propaganda horror stories was of Iraqi soldiers pillaging Kuwaiti hospitals and tossing 312 babies from incubators. The Washington Post carried references to this fantasy some ten times during the Gulf crisis.
cap. 10, sec. Celebrating the Massacre of Iraq
Bombardeo de Irak presentado como espectáculo limpio
Over 90 percent of the bombings involved free-falling gravity bombs that hit anything standing or moving with a total of 85,000 tons of explosives, or the equivalent of seven Hiroshima atomic bombs.
cap. 10, sec. Celebrating the Massacre of Iraq
